name: diesel_i4_4l5_turbo
source: Plausible 4.5 L 4-cylinder turbo-diesel of the mid-size tractor class, NOT a specific engine: rated about 100 kW at 2200 rpm, peak 580 N*m at 1500 rpm (torque rise ~32%), matching published brochure ranges for this class (rated 90-105 kW at 2100-2300 rpm, 520-600 N*m at 1400-1600 rpm; e.g. the John Deere PowerTech 4045 / Deutz TCD 4.1 class - verify before citing). Motoring = friction only (unthrottled diesel), fmep ~1.2-2.0 bar scaled by V_d/(4*pi) = 35.8 N*m/bar. Inertia 1.2 kg*m^2 incl. heavy flywheel. PHYS-033 I3. PHYS-033 P4 I4 C12: the throttle channel is now governed by the 'governor' block below (all-speed, with droop) instead of driving fuel demand directly - rated_rpm 2200 and high_idle_rpm 2400 are the full-fuel and zero-fuel ends of the pre-C12 soft_cut taper, carried over unchanged; droop 0.0909 = 200 rpm / 2200 rpm rated is the SAME full-lever droop the pre-C12 soft_cut limiter's 200 rpm band gave over its 2200-2400 taper (ISO 3046-4 defines droop as the no-load-to-rated speed rise referred to rated speed - here computed from this file's own prior soft_cut band, not an independently measured curve). The limiter is switched from soft_cut to fuel_cut (rpm 2650, hysteresis_rpm 100 - a plain overspeed cutoff placed above the governor's own regulation range) because a governor block already reproduces the soft_cut band's taper shape at full lever; keeping both would apply the droop twice (see docs/data_formats/engine.md's governor section). 2650 rpm and its 100 rpm hysteresis are arbitrary placements clear of the governor's full-lever droop band [2200, 2400] (band = 0.0909*2200 = 200 rpm), not a cited overspeed figure for this engine class.
